one_line: Recent AI developments introduce local analog circuit design tools, physics-constrained chaotic system models, search-native pretraining, RL-based unlearning for corrupted SFT data, and a new looped multimodal mini model.

stories.title: SLIC Technique Enables Local Analog Circuit Design on Laptops
stories.summary: MIT researchers developed SLIC, a small language model technique that performs analog circuit design locally using only a few billion parameters. Running locally protects proprietary company data and eliminates the privacy risks associated with cloud-hosted models.
stories.why_it_matters: Engineers can design analog circuits locally on a laptop without risking data privacy by using cloud-hosted models.
stories.editor_reason: SLIC training method enables a small LLM to efficiently design analog circuits.

facts.claim: MIT researchers developed a new technique called SLIC that allows a small language model to perform analog circuit design locally on a laptop.
facts.quote: The MIT method, called Small LM Iterating on Circuits, or SLIC (pronounced “slick”), enables engineers to train a small language model to perform analog circuit design as well as or better than a frontier large language model (LLM).

facts.claim: The SLIC technique protects proprietary company data and eliminates privacy risks by running locally instead of on resource-intensive cloud-hosted models.
facts.quote: Because it’s trained and deployed locally, it can use a company’s circuit design data without raising privacy risks.

facts.claim: The SLIC model is several thousand times smaller than frontier models, utilizing only a few billion parameters compared to trillions.
facts.quote: The SLIC model uses a few billion parameters, making it several thousand times smaller than frontier models that use trillions of parameters and require enormous amounts of computational resources.

facts.claim: The research will be presented at the upcoming 2026 Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems.
facts.quote: The research will be presented at the 2026 Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems.

first_issues.problem: The facts do not state that analog chips can be designed faster or less expensively.

stories.title: New Method Enforces Physics-Based Restrictions on AI Models
stories.summary: MIT researchers developed a new method using energy-based constraints and a projection layer to restrict machine learning models. This approach prevents models of chaotic systems from producing physically impossible, unbounded predictions over time.
stories.why_it_matters: You can deploy machine learning models for chaotic systems with a mathematical guarantee that their predictions remain physically bounded.
stories.editor_reason: New physics-informed constraints make AI models of chaotic systems reliably consistent.

facts.claim: Researchers at MIT developed a new method to enforce physics-based restrictions on machine learning models.
facts.quote: researchers with MIT’s Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems (LIDS) have found a way to introduce physics-based restrictions on machine learning models

facts.claim: The new approach prevents chaotic system models from producing physically impossible, unbounded predictions over time.
facts.quote: ensure that such models never exceed realistic bounds, based on what is actually possible in the real world.

facts.claim: The research team includes MIT graduate student Sunbochen Tang and professors Navid Azizan and Themistoklis Sapsis.
facts.quote: published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS) in a paper by MIT graduate student Sunbochen Tang and MIT professors Navid Azizan and Themistoklis Sapsis.

facts.claim: The method uses energy-based constraints and a projection layer to guarantee that model predictions remain bounded.
facts.quote: We then add a projection layer, a component that adjusts how the model predicts the system will evolve, to enforce energy dissipation as a hard constraint.

stories.title: Search-Native Pretraining Integrates Search Capabilities Into Language Models
stories.summary: Researchers propose Search-Native Pretraining, which integrates search capabilities during the pretraining phase by augmenting text corpora with web-search queries and responses. The resulting QueryLM models demonstrate better performance on knowledge-intensive tasks and increased evidence steerability.
stories.why_it_matters: Smaller language models can match or outperform larger baseline models on knowledge-intensive tasks by baking search directly into pretraining.
stories.editor_reason: Search-native pretraining integrates retrieval directly into language model pretraining.

facts.claim: Researchers propose Search-Native Pretraining to integrate search capabilities during the pretraining phase using ordinary text corpora.
facts.quote: We propose Search-Native Pretraining as a practical route to teach search capability during pretraining from ordinary text corpora.

facts.claim: The pretraining corpus is augmented with web-search queries and responses retrieved via a local index.
facts.quote: Specifically, we augment pretraining corpus at scale with web-search queries and retrieve web response using a local index.

facts.claim: Search-pretrained models, known as QueryLM, demonstrate better performance on knowledge-intensive tasks and increased evidence steerability across Wikipedia and DCLM-Edu corpora at scales from 360M to 3.3B parameters.
facts.quote: Across Wikipedia and DCLM-Edu corpora and 360M to 3.3B parameter scales, search-pretrained models ("QueryLM") show improved performance on knowledge-intensive tasks and higher steerability toward the retrieved evidence.

facts.claim: A 1.4B parameter QueryLM model matches or outperforms a FLOP-matched 3.3B baseline model on all knowledge-intensive tasks.
facts.quote: we find that a 1.4B QueryLM consistently beats or matches the performance of a FLOP-matched 3.3B baseline model across all knowledge intensive tasks.

stories.title: Reinforcement Learning Restores Reasoning Performance Despite Corrupted SFT Data
stories.summary: Group Relative Policy Optimization post-training successfully restores model reasoning accuracy to gold-baseline levels even when supervised fine-tuning data is severely corrupted. Initializing reinforcement learning with minimal incorrect traces can further boost post-RL performance.
stories.why_it_matters: You can rely on reinforcement learning to discover functional reasoning when your fine-tuning data is compromised.
stories.editor_reason: Reinforcement learning successfully unlearns corrupted supervised fine-tuning in reasoning tasks.

facts.claim: Reinforcement learning succeeds in reasoning tasks even when supervised fine-tuning data is severely corrupted.
facts.quote: reinforcement learning (RL) in reasoning tasks can succeed even when the supervised fine-tuning (SFT) data is severely corrupted

facts.claim: Group Relative Policy Optimization post-training restores model accuracy back to gold-baseline levels of approximately 60% despite data corruption.
facts.quote: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) post-training consistently restores model accuracy back to gold-baseline levels (approximately 60%)

facts.claim: Initializing RL with eight minimal, incorrect, three-line form-only traces boosts post-RL performance to 69.30%.
facts.quote: initializing RL with as few as N = 8 minimal, incorrect, three-line "form-only" traces boosts post-RL performance to 69.30%

facts.claim: SFT accuracy is largely uncorrelated with post-RL accuracy, showing that SFT establishes structural layout while RL discovers functional reasoning.
facts.quote: SFT accuracy is largely uncorrelated with post-RL accuracy (r approximately 0), demonstrating a fundamental asymmetry in post-training: SFT primarily establishes structural layout (form), while RL independently discovers functional reasoning (function).

stories.title: Inkling 2 Mini Released for Local Multimodal AI Setups
stories.summary: Thinking Machines Lab released Inkling 2 Mini, a multimodal Mixture-of-Experts looped transformer featuring 26 billion physical parameters and 3 billion active parameters per token. The model achieves increased capacity by looping middle layers three times and supports a 1-million-token context size.
stories.why_it_matters: You can run a high-capacity, million-context multimodal model locally that processes both image and text inputs efficiently.
stories.editor_reason: Inkling 2 Mini launched for high performance in local AI setups.

facts.claim: Thinking Machines Lab has released Inkling 2 Mini, a new looped transformer model designed for local AI setups.
facts.quote: Inkling 2 Mini is much, much smaller than Inkling 2 Small, and is designed for local AI setups.

facts.claim: Inkling 2 Mini is a multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model featuring roughly 26 billion physical total parameters and 3 billion active parameters per token.
facts.quote: It’s a multimodal Mixture-of-Experts with ~26B physical total and 3B active parameters per token.

facts.claim: The model supports a 1-million-token context size and accepts both image and text inputs.
facts.quote: It supports a 1M-token context size, accepts images and text inputs.

facts.claim: The model achieves its increased capacity by looping 12 middle layers three times, acting as 48 logical layers.
facts.quote: Inkling 2 Mini is a mixture-of-experts model with 24 decoder layers, but the 12 middle layers run three times in a loop.
